about: The Singularity Ladder questbook: ONE source for tools/gen-singularity.js (docs/questbook-integration.md). ASCII only: {6}{l}{r} are section-sign codes, {times} {theta} {u+XXXX} are glyphs, {bom:piece:CH} and {bomdims:piece} are read from structures/manifest.json, and a line '@name' in a text array pastes texts.name. Ids are explicit and recorded in questbook/id-ledger.txt; never reuse or remove one.

chapters.name: Tier 13 - UXV
desc: The Eye's second half. {9}Sirius B{r} (T5) cools white dwarfs into black ones, and {9}the magnetar{r} (T6) runs on Antipolarization Agent. The {9}Quasar Engine{r} and the first galaxies (T7, T8) are here: the quasar's bursts hold the Eye together and power your base.
The bottom rows hold the pack's own UXV parts and machines. The crafted Stargate now waits in {1}The Endgame{r}, after MAX.

chapters.name: Tier 14 - MAX
desc: The last voltage tier. Here: the Supermassive Lattice's L2 tier, the Supermassive Link and the pack's own MAX quests. Coming later: Eye T9 and its {9}White Hole Matter{r}, the MAX parts built from it, and Eye T10, which makes {9}Universium{r} and opens the pack's Universium line in {1}The Endgame{r}.

chapters.name: The Endgame
desc: The Supermassive Lattice's last tiers: L3, L4, Overdrive and Unbound. Then, coming later with Eye T10: Universium, the pack's MHDCSM line and the crafted Stargate.

placeholderNote: [note]{l}Coming later.{r} This part is not in this build yet, so this quest is a checkbox: tick it to keep the chapter moving. It becomes a real quest in a later update, and a ticked box is then cleared so the real step counts.[/note]

kee_body: As the materials around you achieve transcendental properties, pistons and gases stop being enough. The answer is gravity: a black hole, held in a cage of mirrors and coils and spun fast enough that its ergosphere can be put to work.

The {9}Kerr Ergosphere Engine{r} (KEE) holds the hole and does nothing else: it runs no recipes. The machines that use the hole are the {9}Kerr modules{r}, separate machines standing in the cage's arcs (next quests).
{5}{l}MAKE IT{r} The controller is an {9}Assembly Line{r} recipe: scan a {9}Black Hole Seed{r} in the Scanner to research it. NEI shows the rest.
{5}{l}BUILD{r}
- Hologram Projector, stack 1: Kerr T1, {bomdims:kerr_t1}. Chunk-load all of it.

- The Black Hole Compressor's own Extreme Density Space-Bending Casing, Hawking Radiation Realignment Focus and Naquadah Alloy frames, plus Beyond the Stars' Superradiant Mirrors, Mirror Backing, Ergosphere Field Coils, Beam Focusing Quadrupoles, Beam Dumps, Harmonic Lining and {bom:kerr_t1:E} Bolt Injector Rails. At the hole's height a {9}window band{r} runs round the drum: one Quantum Glass pane (the outer mirror ring's skin, and the governor arc in front of the hole) with the cells behind it left open, so the hole shows from the front. The optional task is the full bill.

- Hatches: 1 laser or up to 2 energy hatches in the governor arc, 1 to {bom:kerr_t1:b} {9}bolt buses{r} (plain input buses) on the cage, and optional BHC Utility Hatches beside them. No maintenance hatch.
- Hologram markers 7 and 8 show where the two module controllers go.
{5}{l}RUN{r} Everything is in the GUI.
1. Put a {9}Black Hole Seed{r} in a bolt bus and press Open: the hole opens at {9}8 SM{r} (solar masses).
2. It bleeds mass as Hawking radiation, {9}3.2 / M{sq} SM a tick{r}. Small holes die fast.
3. The {9}governor{r} fires bolts from the bolt buses to hold your {9}setpoint{r} (2-64 SM at T1):
- Neutronium 1/64 SM, Cosmic Neutronium 1/32, Infinity 1/16, Transcendent Metal 1/8, SpaceTime 1/4 SM a bolt;
- at most 4 / 8 / 16 bolts a tick with Mk I / II / III rails. The {l}lowest{r} rail sets the rate, so upgrade them all together.
4. While open, the hole draws {9}8,388,608 EU/t (1 A UEV){r} of containment. Without power the governor stops; below 2 SM the hole evaporates. The power switch does {l}not{r} stop the hole.
5. A {9}Black Hole Collapser{r} in a bolt bus closes it safely: press Collapse twice (with Auto on, a Collapser is used by itself only while the setpoint is 2 SM).

Open and Auto wait for at least {9}1 SM of bolts{r} (64 Neutronium bolts) in the bolt buses and {9}1 A UEV{r} of containment power: without them the 8 SM hole would evaporate in about 3 s and the Seed would be lost.
[note]Mass sets the modules' bonus: a bigger hole gives more parallels, a smaller one more speed. The controller tooltip has the full block list, and NEI's Multiblock tab previews both tiers.[/note]

[note]HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL: a retrieval task counts only what is in your inventory, and it never takes the items. So keep the part on you, claim the quest, then place it. Every quest that says HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL works this way.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the controller (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).
texts.kee_note_pack: [note]The Black Hole Compressor's recipe is removed. The KEE has its own Assembly Line recipe (scan a {9}Black Hole Seed{r} to research it; NEI shows the rest). Every recipe that consumed a BHC controller (the Spacetime Compression Field Generators, the Compressed Circuit Array) now takes a KEE controller instead. A BHC you already placed keeps working.[/note]
eye_body: So you have made yourself an Eternal DTPF or hopefully a few, and now it is time for the push onwards.

Beyond the Stars replaces TecTech's Eye of Harmony with {9}one Eye that grows from T1 to T10{r}, a band at a time, with a {9}live star{r} at its centre. A star is not a batch recipe: it burns every minute, it must be fed, and it must be held steady.

- Hologram stack 1 is the T1 core, {bomdims:eye_core}. Chunk-load the whole footprint: while any chunk of it is unloaded the Eye is {9}frozen{r} (nothing runs, nothing is lost). T1 is 102 {times} 80 blocks, T6 158 {times} 149, T8 196 {times} 218, and the controller stands at one end, so a loader on its chunk alone is not enough.

- It is mostly TecTech's own Eye blocks: {bom:eye_core:U} Reinforced Spatial and {bom:eye_core:Q} Reinforced Temporal Structure Casings (the Condensate Assembler makes these 32 at a time here), Infinite SpaceTime Energy Boundary Casing, Quantum Glass and the three field generator families. At the star's height the core band's front segments are a {9}window{r}: one Quantum Glass pane with the cells behind it left open, and later tiers leave an opening in their arms and rim in front of it, so the star shows from the front.
- On the plinth: gas input hatches for Hydrogen and Helium, an input bus for Stellar Ignition Charges, an ME Output Bus, an ME Output Hatch and a maintenance hatch.
- Power is {9}wireless EU only{r}, and none of it comes back: the Eye makes matter, not power.
{5}{l}LIGHT IT{r} Put {9}Star Chart: Sol{r} in the controller slot (never consumed). Sol lights when:
- a {9}Stellar Ignition Charge{r} is in a plinth input bus;
- the buffers hold {9}600,000,000 L each of Hydrogen and Helium{r}: 10 cycles of upkeep (kept) plus the 100,000,000 L seed cloud (burned);
- the wireless network holds 10 cycles of EU, which the ignition spends.
The protostar contracts for about 40 seconds, then lights.

{5}{l}RUN{r} Every {9}60 s cycle{r} Sol burns {9}50,000,000 L Hydrogen + 50,000,000 L Helium{r} and {9}1.51 {times} 10{sup11} EU{r} (about 1 A UMV), and makes {9}50,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma{r} (NEI: Condensed Raw Stellar Plasma Mixture; the Eye's GUI says Raw Star Matter) into the ME output hatch. Upkeep is paid in full in every zone; a bad zone only cuts the yield.

{5}{l}AUTOMATE{r} Inputs drain into internal buffers every second, so ME stocking input hatches on the gas sockets work. Keep a few charges in the plinth bus from an ME Interface. A dimension display block in the slot runs planets instead (see {c}Planets on the Eye{r}).

If a block breaks or every maintenance issue opens, GT switches the Eye off; it switches itself back on once the structure is whole (or the maintenance fixed) and the star relights from a charge. A soft mallet's off stays off.
[warn]{l}The tier gate:{r} Spacetime Compression decides the tier. An Eye of tier N needs every compression generator at tier N or higher. Crude runs T1.[/warn]
[note]The next quests teach the stability field, planets and the road to T2. The controller tooltip and GUI carry every number.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the controller, Star Chart: Sol and an Ignition Charge (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL: a retrieval task counts only what you carry, so claim before you place them).
gate_pattern: In Beyond the Stars the three generator families do three jobs:
- {9}Spacetime Compression is the hard gate.{r} An Eye of tier N needs every compression generator at tier N or higher. It also decides which planets run.
- {9}Time Dilation{r} above the star's tier opens the time dial (see {c}The Time Dial{r}).
- {9}Stabilisation{r} calms the star: noise and events shrink 5 % per tier above the first.
The families mix freely, and the {l}lowest{r} of each family counts. The hologram places compression at the trigger stack's tier and never downgrades a generator already placed.

{5}{l}TIER STEP{r} You do not re-craft. In the {9}Condensate Assembler{r} a generator of the tier below plus only what the new tier adds (NEI shows it) becomes the next tier: its Kerr controller, casing and singularity cells stay inside. A {9}Stabilisation{r} generator takes one {9}Spacetime Compression{r} and one {9}Time Dilation Retrofit Kit{r} of the new tier (built on a Retrofit Frame from the same parts) for the two generators it holds. Same time as a fresh craft, only cheaper.
{5}{l}CIRCUITS{r} Every generator takes UXV circuits, more at each tier. Any UXV circuit fits; from Eye T4 the {9}Empyrean Mainframe{r} is the far cheaper one (see {c}Empyrean Circuits{r}).
texts.hold_core: {2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the core and the chart (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL: claim before the core goes into escrow).

quests.name: {9}{l}{n}Kerr Compressor Module
desc: The Black Hole Compressor's job, done beside a real black hole. The module is its {9}own machine{r} in the KEE's south arc, with its own GUI and hatches, so nothing on the KEE changes when you use it.
{5}{l}BUILD{r}
- Place this controller where the KEE's hologram shows {9}marker 7{r}, facing out of the cage.
- Project the arc from the module's own controller ({bomdims:kerr_compressor}, one tier).
- {bom:kerr_compressor:c} arc sockets take input buses or hatches, output buses or hatches, and 1 laser or up to 2 energy hatches. No maintenance hatch.

{5}{l}RUN{r} GT's Compressor and Neutronium Compressor recipes. It has no mode switch and needs no programmed circuit: it runs whichever of the two recipe types matches its inputs. It runs only while the KEE's hole is {9}open{r}. When the hole closes it pauses, keeps its recipe and resumes when the hole reopens.
The hole sets the bonus when a recipe starts:

- {9}parallel 8 {times} tier {times} floor(sqrt M){r}, where the tier is that of the module's {l}total{r} input (voltage {times} amps): a 2 A UIV hatch counts as tier 12, so 384 at 16 SM and 768 at 64 SM;
- {9}speed {times} (3200 / M) / 50{r}, between 1 and 4: {times}4 at 16 SM or less, {times}1 at 64 SM or more.
The module costs the hole nothing.
{5}{l}AUTOMATE{r} Plain GT: ME input and output buses. The module's GUI says why it waits (hole closed, KEE not formed, KEE not loaded).
[note]At Kerr T2 it also runs {9}Kerr Densification{r}, which needs a hole of at least 128 SM (UMV chapter).[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the module controller (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {9}{l}{n}Kerr Extractor Module
desc: The east arc's machine: GT's {9}Extractor{r} recipes, items only, beside the same hole.
{5}{l}BUILD{r}
- Place the controller where the KEE's hologram shows {9}marker 8{r}, facing out of the cage.
- Project the arc from it ({bomdims:kerr_extractor}).
- {bom:kerr_extractor:x} sockets: at least 1 input bus, 1 output bus, and 1 laser or up to 2 energy hatches. Item buses only.

{5}{l}RUN{r} Like the compressor: open hole only, the same parallel and speed bonus, and it pauses without losing its recipe. Either module is a good start, and both can run off one hole; Hyperdense Stellar Mixture later needs the {9}Compressor Module{r}.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the module controller (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {9}{l}{n}Feeding the Governor
desc: A hole is cheap to {9}hold{r} and expensive to {9}grow{r}. The bleed is 3.2 / M{sq} SM a tick:
- a fresh 8 SM hole loses 3.2 Neutronium bolts' worth a tick, so Mk I rails on Neutronium barely gain;
- at 16 SM it costs about 0.8 Neutronium bolts a tick (16 a second);
- at 64 SM, about 1 a second.
Without bolts a 16 SM hole lives about 21 seconds, and a 64 SM hole about 23 minutes.
The governor fires bolts in bus and slot order, only as many as cover the shortfall. All five bolt types work and mix freely. Heavier bolts grow a hole faster at the same rail cap.
{5}{l}AUTOMATE{r}
- Stock the bolt buses from ME: an ME Interface, or an export bus on each bus. The GUI shows how long the stock lasts.

- {9}Auto{r} (on by default, in the GUI's Hole control panel): a Seed in a bolt bus opens a closed hole once at least 1 SM of bolts and containment power are there, and a Collapser closes an open hole only while the setpoint is at its minimum, 2 SM (redstone 1 on a setpoint Directive Hatch, or setSetpoint(2)).
- BHC Utility Hatches on the cage give redstone while the hole is open. Invert it into an export bus holding Seeds, and a hole that evaporates reseeds itself.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold 64 Neutronium bolts (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}The Stability Field
desc: A live star is not a recipe. Every second the Eye updates a {9}stability field{r}. At T1 it has one gauge, {9}P{r} (pressure balance): minus is collapse, plus is expansion, and {9}0 is the target{r}. Each higher star adds a gauge.
{5}{l}ZONES{r} The worst gauge sets the zone, the yield and Integrity:
- {9}Resonant{r} within {pm}10: yield {times}1.25, Integrity +1 a second
- {2}Stable{r} within {pm}40: {times}1.00, +0.2
- {5}Strained{r} within {pm}70: {times}0.50, {minus}0.5
- {c}Critical{r} within {pm}100: no yield, {minus}2
- {4}Breach{r} beyond {pm}100: the star is lost at once
{9}Integrity{r} (0-100) at 0 also loses the star. A lost star costs the star and its unfinished cycle, {l}never{r} blocks, cores or unlocked tiers. Relight it with a new charge.

{5}{l}TRIM{r} Pour trim fluids into the {9}Field sockets{r}: {bom:eye_core:f} plain input hatches on the core band. They are never buffered, and ME stocking hatches there are refused. At T1, 1,000 L Helium is {9}P {minus}2{r} and 1,000 L Hydrogen is {9}P +2{r}, up to 10 units a second.

{5}{l}SENSE{r} A {9}Stellar Field Sensor Hatch{r} ({bom:eye_core:n} sockets on the core band) reads one channel against a threshold and emits redstone on all sides: digital (15 above or below the threshold) or analog (0-15 across the range). Channels: P, {theta}, {omega}, {Pi}, the Agent shield, Integrity, Stability, zone, event warning (+, {minus} or any) and upkeep OK. Right-click it to set it up.
{5}{l}AUTOMATE{r} The standard rig:
- a sensor on {9}P > +10{r} {to} a Fluid Regulator cover, or an ME fluid export bus with a redstone card {to} Helium into a Field hatch;
- a second sensor on {9}P < {minus}10{r} {to} Hydrogen.
Covers on the sensor's own side work, wireless redstone transmitters included, so one sensor can drive a valve anywhere.

[note]Sol settles at about P +35 (Stable) by itself, so T1 runs unattended; the rig earns the {times}1.25. Higher stars do {l}not{r} settle. A {9}Directive Hatch{r} in a sensor socket gives the whole rig as one binary code instead, and OpenComputers (bts_eye) can drive it too.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a sensor hatch. Here is a second one for the rig.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Planets on the Eye
desc: Planets are still {9}batch runs{r}, as TecTech ran them. They give TecTech's ores and plasmas, but {l}no{r} Raw Stellar Plasma or dwarf matter: those come only from stars now.
- Put the planet's dimension display block in the controller slot.
- By Eye tier: {9}T1{r} rocket tiers 0-3, {9}T2{r} 4-6, {9}T3{r} 7-8, {9}T4{r} the Deep Dark.
- A tier N Eye runs every planet of tiers 1..N, at {9}{times}2 parallel per tier above{r} the planet's.
- Each compression tier above the planet's TecTech tier takes 3 % off the time.
- EU comes from wireless when a run starts.
[warn]One target per Eye: selecting a planet puts your star out. A second Eye for planets keeps the star burning.[/warn]
A star does not light while a planet run is in progress; it lights when the run ends.
[note]One Deep Dark run on the same Eye is a T4 {to} T5 milestone.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you tick the box: this one is information only.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Harmonic Lock
desc: Hold {9}Resonant for 600 seconds in a row{r} and the Eye locks in: {9}yield {times}1.5{r} until the streak breaks. The GUI's {l}Lock{r} bar counts it, n/600.

Every milestone's Resonant time counts {l}real{r} seconds, so the time dial cannot shortcut it. A tidy rig is how you climb: tighter sensor thresholds (around {pm}5) keep a star inside {pm}10 more of the time.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} your Eye's GUI shows Lock at 600/600 or more and the yield Y at 1.50; then tick the box (a state is not an item).

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Kerr T2: The Density Upgrade
desc: Kerr T2 is the same KEE, made denser. Right-click the controller with the {9}Kerr Density Upgrade{r}: it is consumed, permanent, and survives a wrench.

{5}{l}BUILD{r} The cage then needs the T2 reinforcement (hologram stack 2, {bomdims:kerr_t2}): {bom:kerr_t2:O} Bastion Plates, {bom:kerr_t2:P} Casimir Plates, more Harmonic Lining and more glass. The optional task is exactly the difference. A T2 Kerr with the reinforcement torn down will {l}not form{r}.
{5}{l}WHAT YOU GET{r}
- setpoints up to {9}512 SM{r}, so more module parallels (floor(sqrt M) is 22 at 512 SM, against 8 at 64 SM);
- {9}Kerr Densification{r} on the Compressor Module, with a hole of {9}at least 128 SM{r}.

{5}{l}MAKE IT{r} In the Condensate Assembler (NEI: Condensate Assembling). The big costs are {9}4,000,000 L Entangled Raw Star Matter{r} (Raw Stellar Plasma, condensed 1 : 1; NEI: Condensate Entanglement) and {9}32 Black Hole Seeds{r}, so your T1 Eye pays for it. NEI has the whole recipe.
[note]Growing a hole to 512 SM takes a lot of bolts: SpaceTime bolts (1/4 SM each) and Mk III rails do it fastest.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the upgrade (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Eye T2: Sirius A
desc: Sirius A is a hotter, younger star, and it pushes back. Every tier unlocks in order, in the same three steps:
1. {9}milestones{r} on the current star;
2. {9}the core{r}, right-clicked into escrow;
3. {9}the transition{r}, a live event you have to survive.
{5}{l}MILESTONES{r} On Sol: {9}20,000,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma{r} made and {9}2 h Resonant{r} (real time). The GUI and scanner count them, and they stay with the controller through a wrench.

{5}{l}CORE{r} Right-click the controller with the {9}Stellar Mass Core{r} (Condensate Assembler, 256,000 L Entangled Raw Star Matter). It is consumed {l}only{r} when the transition succeeds. Sneak-punch with an empty hand to take it back.

{5}{l}MASS INFUSION{r} Build the {9}beam band{r} (hologram stack 2: {bom:eye_beam:R} Beam Band Casing) and bring compression to tier 2. Buffer {9}5,000,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma{r} plus Sirius A's first cycle, then put {9}Star Chart: Sirius A{r} in the slot while Sol burns. For 10 minutes the plasma pours into Sol and P is pushed {9}+4 a second{r}, so your rig must hold. Survive it and Sol becomes Sirius A, with T2 unlocked for good. Fail and you lose Sol and the plasma, never the core.

{5}{l}RUN{r} Each cycle: {9}12,500,000 L Hydrogen + 12,500,000 L Helium + 25,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma{r} and 6.04 {times} 10{sup11} EU (about 1 A UXV), for {9}2,500 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture{r}. A relight takes a charge and a 200,000,000 L seed of each gas.
{5}{l}TRIMS{r} As Sol (Helium P {minus}2, Hydrogen P +2 per 1,000 L), now up to 20 units a second. The beam band's {bom:eye_beam:s} stellar sockets take input hatches for the star's fluids.

[warn]Sirius A drifts P +2 a second and breaches if left alone: run the rig. Helium leaves {l}ash{r}, {minus}0.5 % yield per 1,000 L dosed that second, so a two-stage rig (small doses near 0, big ones far out) beats full-blast valves.[/warn]
[note]A higher Eye still hosts lower stars, at {times}2 parallel per tier above. There is one live star per Eye.[/note]
If the Mass Infusion fails, leave the chart in: the Eye relights Sol from a Stellar Ignition Charge and tries again (the core stays in escrow).
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have held the core and the chart before the core goes into escrow (that task latches), and then 1,000 L of Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture, Sirius A's first product.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Eye T3: Arcturus
desc: Arcturus is a red giant: a helium core inside a hydrogen shell. It brings a second gauge, {9}{theta} (core heat){r}, which runs away on its own, and P now climbs with {theta}.
{5}{l}UNLOCK{r}
- Milestones on Sirius A: {9}1,000,000 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture{r} and {9}3 h Resonant{r}.
- The {9}Shell-Burning Core{r} in escrow (Condensate Assembler, 128,000 L Entangled Excited Stellar Plasma).
- The {9}jet crescent{r} built (stack 3: {bom:eye_jet:S} Jet Crescent Casing; the beam band must stand too) and compression at tier 3.
- {9}250,000 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture{r} buffered, plus Arcturus's first cycle.
Then swap in {9}Star Chart: Arcturus{r}.

{5}{l}SHELL IGNITION{r} (10 min) {theta} appears at 0 and ramps in. The T3 trims below, Super Coolant included, work from the start. It ends in one {9}forced helium flash{r} at 600 s, warned at 585 s: pre-cool and ride it.

{5}{l}RUN{r} Each cycle: {9}12,500,000 L Hydrogen + 12,500,000 L Helium + 1,250 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture{r} and 2.42 {times} 10{u+00b9}{sq} EU (about 1 A MAX), for {9}625 L Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma{r}.
{5}{l}TRIMS{r} Up to 20 units a second each:
- Helium (1,000 L): P {minus}1, {theta} +3;
- Hydrogen (1,000 L): P +3, {theta} +0.5;
- Super Coolant (100 L): P {minus}1, {theta} {minus}3.
To pull P down without heating the core, dose Helium {l}and{r} coolant together. Add a sensor pair on {theta} driving the coolant.
{5}{l}HELIUM FLASHES{r} Every 20-40 minutes a flash adds {9}{theta} +30 a second for 3 s{r}. The sensor's event channel warns {9}15 s ahead{r}: pre-cool on the warning and you stay Stable.
If the Shell Ignition fails, leave the chart in: the Eye relights Sirius A from a Stellar Ignition Charge and tries again (the core stays in escrow).
[note]The T3 {to} T4 milestones: {l}400,000 L{r} Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma, {l}4 h Resonant{r}, and {l}3 flashes ridden{r} (never worse than Stable from the warning until 30 s after).[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have held the core and the chart before the core goes into escrow (that task latches), and then 1,000 L of Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Hyperdense Stellar Mixture
desc: Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma is too loose to seed a neutron star, so finish it inside a black hole. The Kerr Compressor Module runs {9}Kerr Densification{r}, only on a {9}Kerr T2 holding at least 128 SM{r}:
- {9}10,000 L Raw Hyperdense Stellar Plasma + 288 L molten SpaceTime + 64 Neutronium bolts {to} 1,000 L Hyperdense Stellar Mixture{r}, 20 s at UMV, before the hole's bonus.
Hyperdense Stellar Mixture (HSM) is used for:
- the Core Collapse's neutron seed (5,000 L);
- feeding the neutron star (0-1.5 L/s);
- the Galactic Upgrade Core (32,000 L, as its condensate);
- Galactic Shell Plating and Star Chart: Neutron Star.
[note]Raise the KEE's setpoint to 128 SM or more before you start: below that the module refuses the recipe.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold 1,000 L of Hyperdense Stellar Mixture.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Eye T4: Core Collapse
desc: Fast-forward a red giant into a {9}neutron star{r}, and stop it going supernova. The Core Collapse is the hardest event yet: read all of this before you start.
{5}{l}BEFORE{r}
- the T3 milestones;
- the {9}Galactic Upgrade Core{r} in escrow (Condensate Assembler, 32,000 L Entangled Hyperdense Stellar Mixture);
- the {9}spiral arms{r} built (stack 4: {bom:eye_arms:T} Galactic Shell Plating) and compression at tier 4;
- Arcturus lit and Stable;
- buffered: {9}5,000 L HSM{r} (the seed), up to {9}90,000 L molten SpaceTime{r} (the shock absorber) and the neutron star's first cycle;
- {9}94,000 L Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid{r} on hand for the Field sockets.
Then swap in {9}Star Chart: Neutron Star{r}.

{5}{l}1 FAST-FORWARD{r} (about 16 min) Dose Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid into the Field sockets, up to 100 L/s. The core climbs from 0.50 to {9}1.44 SM{r} over 94,000 L. The envelope swells P and {theta} as it goes, and your T3 rig must hold.
{5}{l}2 BOUNCE{r} The HSM becomes the neutron seed, Integrity drops 20, and a shock of {9}+150{r} hits P and {theta}.
- Every {9}1,000 L molten SpaceTime{r} buffered cancels 1 point, up to 90: the shock is then +60.
- Any gauge above +100 after the shock is {c}{l}SUPERNOVA{r}: Arcturus, the Time fluid, the HSM and the SpaceTime are lost. The core stays in escrow.
So bring P and {theta} {l}below +40{r} before the bounce. The scanner predicts both.
{5}{l}3 SETTLE{r} The neutron star lights at P 0, {theta} +60, {omega} +30. Get it Stable for 60 seconds in a row within 180 s (Super Coolant pulls {theta} down). T4 is then yours.
{5}{l}THE NEUTRON STAR{r}
- No fusion, so no Hydrogen or Helium: {9}144 L molten SpaceTime{r} a cycle and 9.66 {times} 10{u+00b9}{sq} EU (about 4 A MAX) hold it.
- Set the {9}HSM feed{r} in the GUI (0-1.5 L/s, default 0.694). {9}White Dwarf Matter = 3.6864 L per L of HSM fed{r}, about 9,200 L an hour at the default.
- The feed pushes P, {theta} and the spin {9}{omega}{r} up. {omega} runs away by itself, and {9}glitches{r} kick it +20 every 15-30 minutes {l}without warning{r}.

- Trims, up to 10 units a second: Spatially Enlarged Fluid (100 L) P {minus}2; molten SpaceTime (100 L) P +2; Super Coolant (100 L) {theta} {minus}3; molten Purified Tengam (36 L, up to 5) {theta} +1, {omega} {minus}4.

- If it breaches, it collapses into a black hole. With T4 unlocked, a dark Eye holding the Neutron Star chart relights Arcturus from a charge and reruns the Core Collapse by itself, with no core. Keep the Time fluid, HSM and SpaceTime stocked for it.
[note]The Deep Dark planet runs at T4, and one Deep Dark run is a T4 {to} T5 milestone.[/note]
@hold_core

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}The Homogeny
desc: A mega mixer: a glass mixing column wrapped in a shear helix, inside a spiral volute with three feed vessels. It turns {9}Raw Stellar Plasma into Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture at 100 : 1{r}, with no gases, no ignition and no stability field to watch.
{5}{l}BUILD{r}
- Project it from the controller at the tip of the volute's discharge throat (hologram stack 1 = T1, {bomdims:homog_t1}).
- A fluid Input Hatch on top of each Feed Vessel (3 at T1), an Output Hatch on the throat, and an Energy or Laser Hatch on the bottom cap rim. No maintenance hatch.
- A missing block, or a footprint chunk that is not loaded, pauses the machine: the run is kept and resumes by itself when the structure is whole. Chunk-load the whole footprint.
{5}{l}RUN{r} {9}100,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma {to} 1,000 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture{r} in 240 s at UMV: 1 parallel, no overclock.

Turns stockpiled Raw Stellar Plasma into Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture unattended: no hydrogen, helium, ignition or field. It costs 100 L per 1 L, 10{times} the Raw Stellar Plasma an Eye T2 needs, so it suits banking a Sol surplus or a hands-off line, not replacing Sirius A.
{5}{l}AUTOMATE{r} Plain GT: ME input hatches on the vessels, an ME output hatch on the throat.
[note]It does {l}not{r} skip T2: Eye T2 is still required, and only an Eye hosting Sol makes Raw Stellar Plasma.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the Homogeny controller and 1,000 L of Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}The Time Dial
desc: {9}Time Dilation{r} generators above the star's tier open the {9}time dial m{r}: a speed-up for the whole star.
- The cap is {9}1 + 0.25 {times} (lowest Time Dilation tier {minus} star tier){r}, at most {times}3.00.
- Each +0.25 costs {9}10 {times} 2^(N{minus}1) L/s of Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid{r} (N = the star's tier), drawn from the Field sockets. Paid short, the dial runs slower.
- m speeds up everything the star does (upkeep, product, EU, drift, noise and events) but {l}not{r} your trims. A faster star is harder to hold.
{9}Stabilisation{r} generators calm the star: noise and event size {times} (1 {minus} 0.05 {times} (lowest tier {minus} 1)), down to {times}0.60 at tier 9.
Set the dial with the GUI's {minus} / + buttons (right-click: four steps). It is held at {times}1 during transitions, and milestone Resonant time counts real seconds, not dial seconds.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold 1,000 L of Tachyon Rich Temporal Fluid.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Stellar Silicon
desc: Your Sol's Raw Stellar Plasma grows the first wafer that is not GregTech's: the {9}Stellar Boule{r}. Every wafer of Beyond the Stars' three circuit families starts here, and so does every Stellar SMD.
{5}{l}MAKE IT{r}

- Electric Blast Furnace at {9}12,600 K{r} (Infinity coils on UIV power reach it), 60 s at UIV: an Optically Enriched Crystalline Boule, 4 Shirabon dust, 1 SpaceTime dust and {9}1,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma{r} {to} 1 Stellar Boule.
- Cut it in a Cutting Machine in a cleanroom, 50 s at UEV: {9}16 Stellar Wafers{r} with Grade-7 purified water, {9}24{r} with Grade-8.
Plain GregTech machines, so a normal AE2 pattern runs each step.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a Stellar Boule and 16 Stellar Wafers.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Sidereal Circuits
desc: {c}{l}UMV, FAR CHEAPER{r} The {9}Sidereal{r} circuits are Beyond the Stars' own UHV to UMV line, printed on your star's matter. They fill {l}any{r} circuit slot of their tier in every recipe, and they are {9}far cheaper{r}: a Sidereal Mainframe costs about a fourteenth of the EU of a Pico Circuit (about a thirtieth while Beyond the Stars raises the Pico Circuit's price, which it does by default). No step runs above UMV power.
{5}{l}THE CHAIN{r}

- Stellar Wafer {to} Laser Engraver (Mysterious Crystal lens, it stays in the bus; {9}250 L Raw Stellar Plasma{r}; 30 s at UIV) {to} {9}Sidereal Wafer{r} {to} Cutting Machine {to} {9}8 Sidereal Chips{r} (12 with Grade-8 water).
- Boards: 4 Optical Circuit Boards, Shirabon foil, Hypogen fine wire and Mutated Living Solder {to} 4 Sidereal Circuit Boards (Assembler). No star matter, so you can stock them early.
- {9}Processor{r}: a chip, 2 Optically Compatible Memory and Optical SMDs in a Circuit Assembler (cleanroom), or a Circuit Assembly Line in assembler mode.
- {9}Assembly, Supercomputer, Mainframe{r}: Assembly Line recipes. Research the member below in a {9}Research Station{r} for the data stick.
{5}{l}THEY COUNT AS{r} Processor = UHV, Assembly = UEV, Supercomputer = UIV, {9}Mainframe = UMV{r}.

{5}{l}WHERE THEY GO{r} Anywhere a recipe asks for any UMV circuit: GregTech's UMV parts, hulls and hatches, the Space Elevator parts, and Beyond the Stars' own cores, pylons and charts. NEI cycles them with the stock ones. Nothing asks for Sidereal by name, so a Pico Circuit still fits everywhere. In a {9}computer rack{r} the Mainframe gives 280 computation, slightly better than a Pico Circuit.
[note]Eye T1 itself is still built from Pico Circuits: Sidereal needs your star first.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a Sidereal Processor and a Sidereal Mainframe.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Stellar SMDs
desc: SMD tier 4, above Optical SMDs: the parts that let circuits go past UMV.
{5}{l}MAKE THEM{r} Assembler, cleanroom, 20 s at UIV: one Stellar Wafer, the kind's foils or fine wire and {9}144 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture{r} make {9}64{r}. NEI shows each kind.
Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture comes from Eye T2 (Sirius A) or from the Homogeny, so this quest opens with either one.
{5}{l}USED BY{r} the Empyrean and Omega circuits. Sidereal circuits use Optical SMDs.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold one of each kind.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Empyrean Circuits
desc: {c}{l}UXV AT UMV POWER{r} The {9}Empyrean{r} circuits, UEV to UXV, printed on White Dwarf Matter from your neutron star. They fill any circuit slot of their tier and are {9}far cheaper{r}: an Empyrean Mainframe costs about a fourteenth of the EU of a Quantum circuit (about a thirtieth while the Quantum circuit's price is raised, the default), and no step runs above UMV power.
{5}{l}THE CHAIN{r}
- Engrave a {9}Sidereal Wafer{r} again: Gravitational Lens, {9}36 L molten White Dwarf Matter{r} and 250 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture, 30 s at UMV {to} {9}Empyrean Wafer{r} {to} 8 Empyrean Chips.
- Boards from Sidereal Circuit Boards (Assembler: SpaceTime and Radox Polymer).
- Processors in the Circuit Assembler; Assembly, Supercomputer and Mainframe on the Assembly Line (Research Station research), with Stellar SMDs.
- Every {9}Empyrean Mainframe{r} is built around one Sidereal Mainframe.

- {9}Two fluids{r} on the engraving: a single-block Laser Engraver has one fluid slot, so engrave in a {9}multiblock{r} (GT's Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver, or any engraver multi with two input hatches).
{5}{l}THEY COUNT AS{r} Processor = UEV, Assembly = UIV, Supercomputer = UMV, {9}Mainframe = UXV{r}.

{5}{l}WHERE THEY GO{r} Anywhere a recipe asks for any UXV circuit: every field generator the Eye is built from and upgraded with, the Field Generator UMV (4 each) and Beyond the Stars' cores from Eye T5 on. A Quantum circuit still fits too. In a {9}computer rack{r} the Mainframe gives 340 computation, slightly better than a Quantum circuit.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold an Empyrean Processor and an Empyrean Mainframe.

quests.name: {c}{l}{n}Circuits in the Nanochip Complex
desc: The Nanochip Assembly Complex can build all three families. It gains {l}no new module{r}: Beyond the Stars' parts go through the modules you already have.
- Chips: the {9}Cutting Chamber{r}.
- Stellar SMDs: the {9}Part Processor{r}.
- Boards: the {9}Board Processor{r}.

- Circuits: the {9}Assembly Matrix{r}. Its Component Assembly Line casing must match the circuit's tier as for GregTech's own: UHV casing for every UHV to UIV member, UEV for the UMV ones, UIV for the UXV ones and UMV for the Omega Mainframe.

Feed it as you feed GregTech's circuits; NEI's Nanochip pages show every recipe. It uses the same EU as the Assembly Line route: the gain is throughput. Beyond the Stars' circuits count toward no calibration.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have read this: tick the box.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Omega Circuits
desc: {4}{l}MAX AT EYE T5{r} The {9}Omega{r} circuits, UIV to MAX, printed on Black Dwarf Matter from Sirius B. They fill any circuit slot of their tier and are {9}far cheaper{r}: an Omega Mainframe costs about a fourteenth of the EU of a Planck circuit (about a thirtieth while the Planck circuit's price is raised, the default), with no Universium, Eternity or Magmatter in it.
{5}{l}THE CHAIN{r}
- Engrave an {9}Empyrean Wafer{r} once more: Forcicium lens, {9}18 L molten Black Dwarf Matter{r} and 100 L Hyperdense Stellar Mixture, 60 s at UMV {to} {9}Omega Wafer{r} {to} 8 Omega Chips.
- Boards from Empyrean Circuit Boards (Assembler: Hexanite, Shirabon, Dimensionally Transcendent Residue).
- Processors in the Circuit Assembler; the rest on the Assembly Line (Research Station research), with Stellar SMDs.
- Every {9}Omega Mainframe{r} is built around one Empyrean Mainframe.
- {9}Two fluids{r} again: engrave in a {9}multiblock{r} laser engraver (GT's Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver, or any engraver multi with two input hatches), not the single block.

{5}{l}THEY COUNT AS{r} Processor = UIV, Assembly = UMV, Supercomputer = UXV, {9}Mainframe = MAX{r}. In a {9}computer rack{r} the Mainframe gives 380 computation, slightly better than a Planck circuit.

[note]The pack's MAX machines and parts still need their own late materials: Eternity and Magmatter (Eye T7), and Universium and MHDCSM, which come with Eye T10 (coming later). Omega only removes the circuit wall.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold an Omega Processor and an Omega Mainframe.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Eye T5: Sirius B
desc: A white dwarf, {9}cooled into a black dwarf{r}. Sirius B burns nothing and has no upkeep: it runs in {9}batches{r}, and your job is to follow a cooling curve.
{5}{l}UNLOCK{r} The T4 milestones: {9}147,456 L White Dwarf Matter{r} from cycles never worse than Stable, {9}4 h Resonant{r}, and {9}one Deep Dark run{r} on this Eye. Then:
- put the {9}Subspace Cooling Core{r} in escrow;
- build the {9}second arms{r} (stack 5: {bom:eye_arms2:T} Galactic Shell Plating) and bring compression to tier 5;
- put {9}Star Chart: Sirius B{r} in the slot. The neutron star goes out: one star per Eye.
{9}First Cooling{r} is your first batch. A mean yield of at least 0.9 with no fracture unlocks T5; fall short and the core stays for another try. The batch's Black Dwarf Matter comes out either way.

{5}{l}BATCHES{r} Each batch takes {9}18,432 L White Dwarf Matter{r} and assembles a white dwarf at {theta} +90. Over {9}2 h{r} ({div} the dial) the cooling setpoint ramps from {9}+90 to {minus}90{r}; at T5 the {theta} gauge reads your error from that setpoint. Output: {9}4,608 L Black Dwarf Matter {times} the batch's mean yield{r}. EU: 3.87 {times} 10{sup13} a cycle (about 16 A MAX).
{5}{l}SUBSPACE COOLING{r} Trims:
- Dimensionally Shifted Superfluid (100 L, up to 10 a second): {theta} {minus}1, P {minus}0.5. The heat sink.
- Raw Stellar Plasma (1,000 L, up to 5): {theta} +3, for an overshoot.
- Helium (1,000 L, up to 10): P +2, accretion pressure.
Decay heat pushes {theta} up the whole way and crystallisation drags P down. Expect about {9}100,000 L of Superfluid a batch{r}.
{5}{l}THE PLATEAU{r} While the setpoint crosses {minus}10..+10 (about 800 s), latent heat adds {9}{theta} +0.15 a second{r}. The event channel warns 15 s ahead.

{5}{l}AUTOMATE{r} {theta} reads the error from the curve, so one sensor pair on {theta} drives the Superfluid valve all batch long; a pair on P drives Helium. Keep White Dwarf Matter stocked for the next charge.
[warn]{l}Fracture{r} (Breach or Integrity 0) ends the batch at 25 % of its output {times} the fraction done.[/warn]
[note]One T4 Eye on the default feed makes about enough White Dwarf Matter for one T5 Eye.[/note]
@hold_core

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Eye T6: SGR 1806-20
desc: SGR 1806-20 is a {9}magnetar{r}, the most magnetic object known. White and black dwarf matter merge into it, and its field has to be untwisted for as long as it lives.
{5}{l}UNLOCK{r} The T5 milestone: {9}6 batches{r} at mean yield 0.9 or better with no fracture. Then:
- put the {9}Magnetar Seed Core{r} in escrow;
- build the {9}galactic rim{r} (stack 6: {bom:eye_rim:T} Galactic Shell Plating) and bring compression to tier 6, with {9}no star lit{r};
- buffer the merger charge: {9}18,432 L White Dwarf Matter + 4,608 L Black Dwarf Matter + 100,000 L Antipolarization Agent{r};
- put {9}Star Chart: SGR 1806-20{r} in the slot.
{5}{l}MAGNETAR MERGER{r} The dynamo winds the polarity {9}{Pi}{r} up by itself (+0.5 a second); no flares yet. Agent doses pull {Pi} back toward 0.

1. {9}Imprint:{r} hold {Pi} inside {9}+60..+70{r} for 120 s in a row, within 600 s. The imprint counts up to +90, but above +70 the field is Critical and Integrity drains 2 a second, so a hold up there loses the magnetar.
2. {9}Release:{r} bring {Pi} back inside {pm}40 within 60 s.
A failure spends the charge and keeps the core.
{5}{l}RUN{r} Each cycle: {9}3,000 L Antipolarization Agent{r} (the constant feed) and 1.55 {times} 10{u+00b9}{u+2074} EU (about 64 A MAX), for {9}15 L Magnetar Matter{r}.

- The merger charge also fills a 60-cycle {9}dwarf-matter reserve{r}. At 10 cycles left the Eye tops it up from the buffers with {9}1,800 L White Dwarf + 450 L Black Dwarf Matter{r}; an empty reserve starves the magnetar. Keep both stocked.
- The Eye gives back {9}12 Purified Tengam dust per 1,000 L{r} of Agent burned, through the ME output bus.
{5}{l}THE FIELD{r} Four gauges: P, {theta}, {omega} and {Pi}, and {Pi} runs away by itself.
- The Agent feed charges the {9}flare shield A{r} (it settles near 40 with no trim). The shield soaks up to 25 {Pi} a second.
- {9}Giant flares{r} come every 60-120 s, warned {9}15 s ahead with their sign{r}, and push {Pi} {pm}25 a second for 4 s.
- Pre-charge the shield on the warning: Agent in a Field socket, 100 L = A +4 ({theta} +0.5), up to 5 a second.
- The other trims are the neutron star's: Spatially Enlarged Fluid, molten SpaceTime, Super Coolant and molten Purified Tengam.
Lose the magnetar and a re-merge needs the charge again, but not the core.
[note]Magnetar Matter is Eye T7's upkeep (7.5 L a cycle) and, later, a base of the T9 pellets. The road on is the {9}Quasar Engine{r}: T7 needs a linked quasar (the {c}Stability Link{r}).[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have held the core and the chart before the core goes into escrow (that task latches), and then 1,000 L of Magnetar Matter.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}The Homogeny T2
desc: The Homogeny's second tier: a middle stirring ring, three more feed vessels and the outer spokes around the same controller. It mixes at {9}4 parallels{r} and adds {9}Degenerate Stellar Mixture{r}: 72 L molten White Dwarf Matter + 72 L molten Black Dwarf Matter + 1,000 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture {to} 1,000 L in 60 s.
{5}{l}UPGRADE{r} (permanent)
- Build the stirring ring: hologram stack 2. Each new vessel takes a fluid Input Hatch on top.
- Mix {9}100,000 L{r} of Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture in this Homogeny.
- Right-click the {9}Homogeny Tier II Core{r} (made in the Condensate Assembler) onto the controller. Sneak-punch with an empty hand returns it.
- Press Install in the GUI, or use a screwdriver: {9}10 minutes offline{r} at UXV power. A mix already running finishes first. Progress shows in the GUI and the scanner, and survives a wrench.
Degenerate Stellar Mixture feeds the Homogeny T3, the Eternity Shell Casing and the Reality machines (Tier 14 - MAX).
Three cells on the stirring ring's outer face take GRB Receptor Ports: a quasar link makes it up to 1.5 {times} faster, 6 {times} the T1 rate (see {c}A Quasar-Held Vortex{r}).

[note]The Tier II Core is built from {9}twice as many UMV parts{r} (32 Field Generators, 64 Electric Pumps) for now: the pack's UXV Field Generator and Pump still need Universium, which comes with Eye T10 (coming later). UXV circuits are fine: any UXV circuit fits, and from Eye T4 the {9}Empyrean Mainframe{r} is the far cheaper one.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a Homogeny Tier II Core and 1,000 L of Degenerate Stellar Mixture (claim before you install the core).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Antipolarization Agent
desc: Tengam with its electrons swapped for positrons is literally {9}antipolarised{r}. Field-cooling it locks the reversed domains, and its counter-currents untwist a magnetar's field.
{5}{l}CHAIN{r}
1. Raw Tengam {to} Electromagnetic Separator {to} Purified Tengam {to} Polarizer {to} {9}Attuned Tengam dust{r}.
2. {9}Large Chemical Reactor{r} (UXV, 20 s): 16 Attuned Tengam dust + 100 L Semi-Stable Antimatter + 144 L molten SpaceTime {to} {9}1,000 L Positronic Tengam Slurry{r}.
3. {9}Vacuum Freezer{r} (UXV, 10 s): 1,000 L slurry + 2,000 L Super Coolant {to} {9}1,000 L Antipolarization Agent{r}.
Semi-Stable Antimatter comes from the Antimatter Forge (SSASS).
{5}{l}USE{r}
- the magnetar's {9}constant feed{r}, 3,000 L a cycle (50 L/s);
- the Magnetar Merger charge, 100,000 L;
- the Magnetar Seed Core, 64,000 L (as its condensate);
- the flare shield trim.
{5}{l}AUTOMATE{r} One reactor at UXV makes 50 L/s, exactly the feed. Run two, chained to the freezer through ME, to cover the shield trims and the next merger charge.
[note]The Eye returns {l}12 dust{r} of Purified Tengam per 1,000 L of Agent burned (75 % of the Tengam), so antimatter is the real cost.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold 1,000 L of Antipolarization Agent.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Quasar Engine
desc: The Quasar Engine is its own black hole with an {9}accretion disc{r}. It runs no recipes: it makes {9}bursts{r} on two jets, measured in {9}Bu/t{r} (burst units per tick: a crown turns 1 Bu/t into 10{sup13} EU/t). A fully grown 4,096 SM quasar on its coils alone makes about 9,796 Bu/t (9.8e16 EU/t, 98 quadrillion). The bursts are for power (the crowns) and for stability (the Eye, the Kerr, the Homogeny, Reality Diffraction).
{5}{l}BUILD{r} Hologram stack 1, {bomdims:quasar}. Chunk-load all of it: an unloaded chunk freezes the disc and pauses every machine it feeds.

- {bom:quasar:E} Eddington Wall Casings, {bom:quasar:H} Disc Field Coils (one tier everywhere), {bom:quasar:C} Jet Collimator Rings and {bom:quasar:I} Rim Gas Injectors, each a batch recipe in the Condensate Assembler (64, 32, 32 and 8 a craft), plus the Black Hole Compressor's own casings for the cage. The optional task is the full bill.
- Nothing in the quasar needs Ergomatter: the Antipolarization Agent takes its place in every recipe you need before Eye T7.

- Hatches: 24 gas sockets on the rim, 4 trim sockets (plain Input Hatches) in the wall tanks, 4 Burst Control sockets on the cap rims, and a control box with up to 3 Energy or Laser Hatches, 2 Directive Hatches, 2 Stellar Field Sensor Hatches and a maintenance hatch.

{5}{l}OPEN{r} Put the {9}Quasar Seed{r} in the controller's slot and press Open in the GUI's Disc panel: a {9}64 SM{r} hole with no spin. Its jets are faint for about an hour while it spins up (the GUI says spinning up). Collapse makes it dormant with its mass kept; a plain Black Hole Seed reopens it. Nothing ever destroys the hole or a block.

{5}{l}THE DISC{r} Helium (or Hydrogen, or Raw Stellar Plasma) into the gas sockets; ME stocking hatches are fine, and the quasar keeps 60 s of feed in its own buffer (counted at f 0.3 at least), so the disc runs on for about a minute after the supply stops. The feed {9}f{r} (GUI, 0-1.5, default 0.85) is a share of the Eddington feed 40 {times} M / {u+03ba} L/s. {u+03ba} is 0.4 for Hydrogen, 0.2 for Helium and 0.1 for Raw Stellar Plasma: at 64 SM on Helium the Eddington feed is 12,800 L/s.

- {9}E{r}, the Eddington balance (aim for 0; starved is negative): Resonant within {pm}10, Stable {pm}40, Strained {pm}70, Critical {pm}100, then a {9}blow-out{r}: no jets for 5 min while the disc re-forms (once f is 0.3 or more). The hole is kept.
- The {9}jet yield{r} follows the zone: 1.25 Resonant (1.5 after 10 min), 1 Stable, 0.5 Strained, 0 Critical.
- Trims into the 4 {9}plain{r} trim hatches: the feed gas (1,000 {times} M/64 L a unit) raises E by 2, Spatially Enlarged Fluid (100 {times} M/64 L) lowers it by 2, at most 10 units a second each.
- The {9}flux{r} (0-100) charges with the field b and erupts at 100: 3 s at 3 {times} the stream. A Burst Control Hatch purges it early (from 20).

- The stream is G0 = {u+03bb} {times} a{sq} {times} b{sq} {times} (M/64){sq} Bu/t ({times} 10{sup13} = EU/t); each jet carries half. Coil power is 2 A UXV {times} b{sq} while the hole is open; without it b is 0, the jets stop and the flux freezes.
- Unattended at {9}f 0.85{r} the disc sits Stable. {9}f 1.0{r} with the two trim valves (riding Eddington) gives about 1.5-1.8 {times} the output, and the links need it.
[note]The NEI page Quasar Engine (accretion disc) shows the Eddington feed per gas. The controller tooltip and the GUI carry every number.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the controller (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL: claim before you place it).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Einstein-Rosen Conduit
desc: The Conduit carries bursts anywhere, with no loss.

- {9}Wormhole Mouths{r}: right-click one with a Data Stick, then the other: they are paired, at any distance, even in another dimension. A stream enters a ring through its front face (the controller's side) and leaves the partner out of its back. To take a jet, lay a mouth on a quasar cap with its front-face centre on the port cell, facing the quasar.
- {9}Mirrors{r} turn a stream 90{deg} (any facing; either throat in).

- {9}Junctions{r} split (the big throat in; out 3 takes its fixed % first; out 1 and out 2 share the rest by c + k {times} (s/15 - 0.5), s from its Burst Control Hatch) or combine (three in, one out).
- A stream flies straight through up to 64 blocks of air to the next throat or a GRB Receptor Port. The scanner names the target, or where it is blocked.

Put a throat in each controller and fuel in its input hatches. A new element opens after 10 s of paid upkeep. One throat caps the whole element; the excess is clipped, never damage. Keep every element chunk-loaded: an unloaded one breaks the path.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold two Wormhole Mouths, a Conduit Mirror and a Conduit Junction (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Eye T7: Triangulum
desc: Triangulum: the first galaxy, and the first tier the quasar holds together. The new verb is {9}aim{r}.

{5}{l}RUN{r} Each cycle: {9}7.5 L Magnetar Matter{r} plus bursts on the rail, for {9}600 L Ergomatter {times} Y {times} r {times} min({u+03b2}, 1.5){r}: Y is the cycle's mean field yield, r the share of the upkeep that arrived, and {u+03b2} the bursts delivered {div} the 1.5 Bu/t (1.5e13 EU/t, 15 trillion) demand.
{5}{l}THE GAUGES{r}

- {9}P{r}, pressure: bursts heat it at 3 {times} ({u+03b2} - 1) a second; Space trims cool it (-2 a unit, up to 10 a second). Aim for about {9}1.5 {times} the demand{r} on average and send the surplus to a crown. The standard rig's J1 sends the Eye everything while P is low and nothing while it is high; its out 1 limit (7.5 Bu/t, 7.5e13 EU/t, per parallel) stops a big quasar flooding the Eye.
- {9}W{r}, the warp of the tilted rail: it drifts 1.5 a second in the precession sense. Aim the bursts between the high and low banks: W moves by 6 {times} (low - high).
- {9}Minor mergers{r} (every 15-30 min, a 15 s warning with the sign) push W {pm}12 a second for 5 s, then flip the precession.

{5}{l}DIRECTIVES{r} The 4 plinth d sockets take Directive Hatches (Field, Events, Galaxy Transition) and a Burst Control Hatch in Begin mode; a Slots hatch can go in a Sensor socket. Each code adds its bits:
- Field: [1] P > +w Space trim, [2] P < -w more bursts, [4] W > +w aim high, [8] W < -w aim low.
- Events: [1] {u+039b} > +w more to the halo, [2] {u+039b} < -w less to the halo, [4] a countdown is running, [8] its sign is minus.
- Slots: [1] a slot is idle, [2] a companion's upkeep is short, [4] a planet run lost parallels, [8] link test fire wanted.
The Galaxy panel (the GUI's galaxy button) sets the mode, the T8 feed and Begin. The terminal shows the bursts, {u+03b2} against the demand, W and the event countdown.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have 1,000 L of Ergomatter.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Ergomatter
desc: Eye T7's harvest. Its uses:
- the Conduit's throat fuel after T7 (0.25 / 1 / 4 L/s per element);
- Eye T8's feed (0-10 L/s);
- the Mk III throat;
- with Beyond the Stars' Eye, the input of the {9}Eternity{r} loop: the Temporal Harmonizer Catalyst takes 9,216 L of Ergomatter and the Plasma Forge's Timepiece 4,608 L, instead of Universium.
A quasar-linked Kerr T2 refines it into Superdense Ergomatter at 8 : 1 (see {c}Superdense Ergomatter, the Slow Way{r}).
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have 16,000 L of Ergomatter.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Eye T8: Milky Way
desc: The Milky Way. You aim a third stream into the shard halo and catch the satellite crossings.

{5}{l}RUN{r} An Ergomatter feed {9}f8 of 0-10 L/s{r} (the Galaxy panel, default 5) makes {9}Superdense Ergomatter = 1.0 {times} the feed {times} Y {times} r{r} (Y the mean field yield, r the share of the upkeep paid).
- {9}{u+039b}{r}, the tidal shear: the feed drives it at 0.4 {times} f8, and halo bursts hold it at -10 {times} the halo share. Wire J3 to Events [1] / [2].

- {9}Satellite crossings{r} (every 30-60 min, an exact 2 min countdown) push P for 5 min. Stay Stable throughout to {9}catch{r} one, for a bonus cycle of Superdense Ergomatter. Run the Space rig, and lower f8 during the countdown at high feed.
T8 is {9}required{r}: no Eye tier can be skipped.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have 1,000 L of Superdense Ergomatter.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Superdense Ergomatter
desc: Ergomatter, compacted. Two routes, one fluid:
- {9}Eye T8{r}: 1 : 1 from its feed, about nine times better;
- {9}the Kerr{r}, before T8: the Compressor Module refines 4,000 L Ergomatter + 1,440 L Molten SpaceTime {to} 500 L in 10 min at UXV (see {c}Superdense Ergomatter, the Slow Way{r}).

It builds the Supermassive Lattice's Containment Nodes (L1 to L4), the Mk IV throat and the Mk IV crown's casing. Coming later, it also feeds the T9 pellets, the Homogeny's Entanglement Medium and Reality Diffraction's Positive Mass anchor (Tier 14 - MAX).
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have 16,000 L of Superdense Ergomatter.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Burst Thermaliser Crown
desc: The quasar's power plant: {9}1 Bu/t {to} 10{sup13} EU/t{r} into your wireless network, no dynamo.

{5}{l}DOCK IT{r} A crown takes a jet when its base centre sits on the quasar's {9}port cell{r}: the cell just past each cap, on the jet axis. Stand it on the top cap; hang it upside down under the bottom cap (wrench the controller's front to turn it). NEI's multiblock preview of the crown shows where its base centre is. A portable scanner on the Quasar Engine prints both port cells, where each crown's controller goes and which way it faces.

{5}{l}MK I, II, III{r} The crown you build around the same controller ({bomdims:crown_mk1} for Mk I): caps of {9}32 / 512 / 8,192 Bu/t{r} (3.2e14 / 5.1e15 / 8.2e16 EU/t: 320 trillion, 5.1 and 82 quadrillion). Build the bigger one around it to upgrade. The bigger Mk does not keep the smaller one's petals and collimators: clear them first (the projector never breaks a block). A crown stacked on top sits higher over a bigger lower crown: re-place it after upgrading the lower one. A second crown stacked on the first takes the overflow. A port with nothing docked vents (Disc [8] lights).
A GRB Receptor Port in its base lets a conduit feed a crown anywhere.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold the controller (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Magnetar-Reinforced Borosilicate Glass
desc: The UXV glass tier for multiblocks that check their glass, made with Magnetar Matter. It belongs to the new UXV parts, which will take Universium out of UXV recipes.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}UXV Superconductor
desc: The pack's superconductors stop at UMV. This UXV one will be drawn from Magnetar Matter, with Antipolarization Agent wherever it is needed before Eye T7. It belongs to the new UXV parts, which will take Universium out of UXV recipes.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}UXV Laser Hatches
desc: The pack's UXV laser source and target hatches carry more power than any energy hatch. They are built from the pack's UXV parts, which need Universium, so they come with Eye T10 (coming later).
[note]On a Kerr module the tier of the total input (voltage {times} amps) sets the parallels: a 256A UXV laser counts as tier 17, so 8 {times} 17 {times} floor(sqrt M).[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a 256A UXV Laser Source Hatch and its Target Hatch.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}A Seed for a Quasar
desc: The Quasar Engine needs its own black hole. A Kerr T2 makes the seed without spending its own hole: {9}4 Black Hole Seeds{r}, {9}64,000 L Hyperdense Stellar Mixture{r} and {9}1,440 L Magnetar Matter{r} in its Compressor Module, with the Kerr Ergosphere Engine (KEE) holding at least {9}256 SM{r}.
The seed opens a 64 SM hole once. A collapsed hole goes dormant and reopens with a plain Black Hole Seed, so you only ever need one.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a Quasar Seed (claim before it goes into the controller).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Disc Field Coils
desc: Tier I-IV: Infinity, Transcendent Metal, SpaceTime, Magmatter. Every coil in a quasar is the same tier; the Condensate Assembler makes 32 a craft.
- The field b is at most the tier. A Burst Control Hatch in b mode sets it from redstone: b = 0.5 + (tier - 0.5) {times} s/15.
- The hole grows to the tier's cap, {9}256 / 1,024 / 2,048 / 4,096 SM{r}, then the GUI says coil cap.
- Coil power is 2 A UXV {times} b{sq}. Without it b is 0: the jets stop and the flux freezes.

Rebuild with a higher tier at any time; the hole is kept. With a lattice standing under a hole over 4,096 SM, coils under Magmatter {9}freeze{r} the quasar (nothing is lost) until Tier IV coils are back: to fit lower coils, lower the mass setpoint to 4,096 SM first. Tier IV's Magmatter comes from the Godforge's magmatter mode: with Beyond the Stars' Eye its EE upgrade costs Black Dwarf Matter frame boxes instead of Universium, so Tier IV arrives at Eye T7. Saturation and the Supermassive Lattice need Tier IV.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold 32 Tier I coils (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Reading the Disc
desc: The control box takes 2 {9}Directive Hatches{r} and 2 {9}Stellar Field Sensor Hatches{r}. The console's E dial is the Eddington balance; the flux bar fills to an eruption at 100 (one tick marks your purge setpoint, another the 90 warning).
{5}{l}QUASAR: DISC{r} The Directive Hatch's set (window w in its GUI, default 5). Each code adds its bits:
- [1] E < -w: pulse the feed gas;
- [2] E > +w: a Space trim;
- [4] the flux at your purge setpoint: purge;
- [8] alarm: a blow-out or re-forming, no coil power, a jet venting, a conduit element closed.

{5}{l}SENSOR{r} E, the flux, {u+03bb}, a, M, Bu/t, the eruption warning, seconds to the next eruption, the best host's {u+03c3} and the link streak: analog with a window, or 15 above / below a threshold; invert flips it.
A comparator reads the Directive code; Steve's Factory Manager reads it as an analog range.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a Directive Hatch (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Burst Control
desc: A {9}Burst Control Hatch{r} reads redstone (strength s, 0-15). Its mode is set in its GUI, and each machine reads only the modes it uses:

- {9}Purge{r} (a quasar cap rim): a rising edge dumps the flux early, from 20 (under 20 it is refused). Never purging averages 1.11 {times} G0 {times} the jet yield; purging at flux 40 about 0.8, but a timed purge makes a spike (see {c}Magnetar Collapse{r}).
- {9}Field b{r} (quasar): b = 0.5 + (coil tier - 0.5) {times} s/15.
- {9}Junction split{r} (a Conduit Junction): out 1's share = c + k {times} (s/15 - 0.5), k 0, 1, 2 or 4.
- {9}Begin{r} (an Eye plinth d socket): a rising edge begins the Magnetar Collapse or the Galactic Merger once Galaxy Transition [1] is on.
- {9}Hold{r} (a quasar with a Supermassive Lattice): sets the mass setpoint (redstone 1 the safe limit .. 15 the band top; 0 leaves the GUI's setpoint, so an unwired hatch changes nothing).
- {9}Overdrive{r} (a quasar on an L3 lattice or better): o = s/15, rounded to 5 % steps.
- {9}Shed{r} (a quasar with a lattice): a rising edge lowers the mass setpoint to the safe limit. A signal that is already on when the server starts is not an edge.
The standard rig: the quasar's Directive Hatch (Disc set) bit [4] AND NOT the Eye's Galaxy Transition bit [8], OR Galaxy Transition [4], into this hatch.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a Burst Control Hatch (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Throats
desc: A {9}throat{r} sits in a Wormhole Mouth, Conduit Mirror or Conduit Junction controller like a turbine rotor. Mk I carries {9}24 Bu/t{r} (2.4e14 EU/t), Mk II 384 (3.8e15 EU/t), Mk III 6,144 (6.1e16 EU/t; it takes Ergomatter: a T7 part) and Mk IV 524,288 (5.2e18 EU/t; see {c}Event Horizon Crown{r}). Anything above is clipped, never damage.

Each element (each mouth of a pair, each mirror, each junction) pays one upkeep unit a second while a throat is fitted, whatever it carries: {9}Molten SpaceTime 4 / 16 / 64 / 256 L/s{r} by throat Mk before T7, {9}Ergomatter 0.25 / 1 / 4 / 16 L/s{r} after. A Mk IV also burns {9}2 L/s Superdense Ergomatter{r}, and prefers it in Auto and Ergomatter modes. The GUI's fuel button picks Auto, SpaceTime or Ergomatter. Short upkeep closes the element; it reopens after 10 s paid.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a Mk I throat (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}A Quasar Link
desc: A {9}GRB Receptor Port{r} takes a stream into a machine: the Eye's rail and halo, a crown's base, a Kerr utility socket, the Homogeny's stirring ring, Reality Diffraction's portal.

A machine is {9}linked{r} while bursts arrived last second from a formed quasar with its hole open and its coils powered, through an open path. Break an element or starve its fuel and the link drops the next second. {u+03c3} = delivered {div} the machine's demand, on a 60 s mean; conditions and bonuses use the mean.

If the quasar's chunk unloads, linked machines {9}pause{r} instead of failing. Keep every Conduit element and Wormhole Mouth on the path chunk-loaded too: an unloaded one stops the stream. The quasar's GUI lists every machine it feeds, with its {u+03c3}. No machine needs a link to work, except a Reality Diffraction with ports fitted.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold a GRB Receptor Port (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}The Stability Rail
desc: Eye band 7, the {9}stability rail{r}, round the galactic rim: hologram stack 7, {bom:eye_rail:B} Bastion Plate with {bom:eye_rail:P} Casimir trim, tilted 8{deg}. Its 8 sockets take {9}GRB Receptor Ports{r}: 4 on the high bank, 4 on the low (T7 needs at least one on each bank).
At T6 the rail's bursts do nothing to the magnetar. They count only for the {c}Stability Link{r}.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold 8 GRB Receptor Ports (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Stability Link
desc: The T6 {to} T7 machine milestone: a linked quasar delivers a 60 s mean of at least {9}1.5 Bu/t{r} (1.5e13 EU/t) to the rail, the high bank taking 25-75 %, for {9}30 min unbroken{r}. The streak resets the second it fails.
{5}{l}THE ORDER{r}
1. The item milestones: 2,700 L Magnetar Matter from all-Stable cycles, 2 h Resonant, 50 giant flares ridden.
2. {9}Transition [4]{r} asks for the {9}Intergalactic Upgrade Core{r}: put it in escrow.
3. {9}Slots [8]{r} asks for the test fire: J1 all to the Eye. At T6 the bursts are a test fire with no field effect.
4. The link, then the Triangulum chart, then Begin (see {c}Magnetar Collapse{r}).

Run the quasar at {9}f 1.0{r} with its trim valves: a 64 SM quasar at the default f 0.85 is too thin, and a fresh hole spins up for about an hour first. The GUI, the scanner, the sensor's link streak and link mean channels, and OpenComputers getUnlock() show the streak.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} the Eye's GUI says the Stability Link is held (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Magnetar Collapse
desc: The T6 {to} T7 transition. With the {9}Intergalactic Upgrade Core{r} in escrow (right-click the controller) and {9}Star Chart: Triangulum{r} in the slot, the Eye is PENDING and the magnetar keeps burning.
{5}{l}BEGIN{r}
- Buffer the charge first: {9}18,432 L White Dwarf Matter{r} and {9}4,608 L Black Dwarf Matter{r} ({times} p), plus Triangulum's first cycle (7.5 L Magnetar Matter: keep at least 8 L).
- When Galaxy Transition [1] (ready) is on, {9}Begin{r}: the GUI's Galaxy panel, a rising edge on a Burst Control Hatch in Begin mode in a plinth d socket, or OpenComputers beginTransition().
{5}{l}PHASES{r}
1. {9}Overfeed{r}, 5 min: White Dwarf Matter 61.44 and Black Dwarf Matter 15.36 L/s on top of the upkeep; {omega} and {Pi} wind up.
2. {9}Collapse{r}: a shock of P +120, minus 10 for every Bu/t (1e13 EU/t) above 1.5 that lands that second.
3. {9}Halo capture{r}, 10 min: Stable for 60 s in a row between 7:00 and 10:00. A minor merger comes at 7:30.

{5}{l}THE SKILL MOVE{r} Land an eruption on the collapse second. Galaxy Transition [8] holds your regulator's purges from T-80 s, and [4] says purge now (at T-80 s if the flux would erupt early, then from T-2 s: an eruption lasts 3 s, so wiring that answers within a second still lands it): wire (Disc [4] AND NOT [8]) OR [4] to the quasar's Burst Control Hatch and the eruption lands on the collapse.

- What it cancels is the quasar's stream: the whole shock needs {9}13.5 Bu/t{r} (1.35e14 EU/t) on the Eye that second. A quasar whose best (a purge at full flux, 3.5 {times} G0 {times} the jet yield) falls short gets a {c}red row{r} above Begin and in the Galaxy panel, with the shock it would leave. Begin still works; grow the quasar first.
A failure loses the magnetar and keeps the core in escrow. Leave the chart in: the Eye re-spawns the magnetar (the Magnetar Merger's charge) and the collapse can run again, with no core and no link.

[note]The core is a Condensate Assembler recipe: Entangled Magnetar Matter, Antipolarization Agent, SpaceTime and Black Dwarf condensates, two Mk I throats and White Dwarf nanites. It is consumed only when the collapse succeeds.[/note]
@hold_core

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}The Shard Halo
desc: Eye band 8, the {9}shard halo{r}: hologram stack 8, {bom:eye_halo:B} Bastion Plate. Its 8 shard roots take {9}GRB Receptor Ports{r}, and the Galactic Merger needs all eight. For T8 the compression generators go to tier 8 (Tipler).
At T7 the halo's bursts are a {9}test fire{r}: they count for the {c}Heavy Link{r} and do nothing to the galaxy.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you hold 8 GRB Receptor Ports (HOLD {to} CLAIM {to} INSTALL).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Heavy Link
desc: The T7 {to} T8 machine milestone: a 60 s mean of at least {9}6 Bu/t{r} (6e13 EU/t) on the Eye's ports, at least half of it on the halo, for {9}30 min unbroken{r}.
{5}{l}THE ORDER{r}
1. The item milestones: 216,000 L Ergomatter from all-Stable cycles, 2 h Resonant, 4 minor mergers ridden.
2. {9}Transition [4]{r}: the {9}Supermassive Seed Core{r} into escrow.
3. {9}Slots [8]{r}: the test fire. J1 all to the Eye, and J3 to its 75 % halo preset.

Slots [8] waits until the quasar's mean stream reaches {9}6 Bu/t{r} (6e13 EU/t) (about 110 SM at coils 3): below that the rail's quarter would starve Triangulum. Keep the quasar growing (f 1.0); the Galaxy panel says how far you are.

With the standard rig's {9}J1 out 1 limit{r} (7.5 Bu/t, 7.5e13 EU/t, per parallel) the test fire puts 7.5 Bu/t on the Eye at any quasar size: 5.6 on the halo, 1.9 on the rail (5.6e13 and 1.9e13 EU/t). Without a limit, Slots [8] stops again above {9}32 Bu/t{r} (3.2e14 EU/t, about 260 SM), as the rail's quarter would flood the field; the Galaxy panel then says to set the limit, or gives J1's Eye share to test-fire with (testFireShare in OpenComputers getUnlock()).
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} the Eye's GUI says the Heavy Link is held (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Galactic Merger
desc: The T7 {to} T8 transition. Put the {9}Supermassive Seed Core{r} in escrow and {9}Star Chart: Milky Way{r} in the slot while Triangulum burns, in galaxy mode with no companion charts in the slot bus. Buffer {9}9,000 L Ergomatter{r} ({times} p) plus the Milky Way's first feed cycle, then {9}Begin{r}.
{5}{l}THE MERGER{r} 30 min:
- the demand ramps from 1.5 to 6 Bu/t (1.5e13 to 6e13 EU/t), and the Ergomatter charge feeds at 5 L/s;
- three warned pericentre passes at 10, 20 and 30 min give W {pm}12 and P +5 a second for 5 s;
- then Stable for 2 min in a row within 5 min.
A failure loses Triangulum and keeps the core; the Eye re-runs the chain from the magnetar.
[note]The core is made from 128,000 L Entangled Ergomatter, 2,304 L Magnetar Matter and Black Dwarf nanites. Its name is the hole it seeds, not the fluid.[/note]
@hold_core

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Superdense Ergomatter, the Slow Way
desc: Before T8, the Kerr Compressor Module refines Ergomatter {9}8 : 1{r}: 4,000 L + 1,440 L Molten SpaceTime {to} 500 L Superdense Ergomatter, 10 min, UXV.

It needs the Kerr Ergosphere Engine (KEE) at T2, holding at least {9}256 SM{r}, with a quasar link at {u+03c3} {ge} 1 (a GRB Receptor Port in a utility socket). A run that loses the link pauses; nothing is voided.
Eye T8 makes the same fluid 1 : 1 from its feed: this route is for before T8.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have 500 L of Superdense Ergomatter.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}A Quasar-Linked Kerr
desc: A {9}GRB Receptor Port{r} fits any Kerr Ergosphere Engine (KEE) utility socket. Demand: 0.1 Bu/t (1e12 EU/t) at T1, 0.25 (2.5e12) at T2; {u+03c3} on the 60 s mean.
- The Hawking bleed is {times} (1 - 0.75 {times} min({u+03c3}, 1)): at {u+03c3} {ge} 1 the hole needs 75 % fewer bolts.
- On T2 at {u+03c3} {ge} 1 the setpoint cap rises from 512 to {9}768 SM{r}, so the modules get 27 parallels instead of 22.

- A lost link drops the cap back to 512. The hole bleeds down to it slowly and your setpoint is kept; the modules count the mass only up to the cap in force, so the extra parallels go with the link at once.
- A quasar that is unformed or not loaded pauses the link: the bleed relief, the 768 SM cap and the Superdense refining stop until it runs again.
- One Junction's out 3 at 10 % feeds a KEE T2 from any quasar of 2.5 Bu/t (2.5e13 EU/t) or more.
The KEE's GUI and scanner show the link line; OpenComputers bts_kerr.getState().link.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} your KEE shows a quasar link (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}A Quasar-Held Vortex
desc: 3 {9}GRB Receptor Ports{r} fit the Homogeny's stirring ring (its reserved cells). Demand: 1.5 Bu/t (1.5e13 EU/t) at T2, 6 (6e13) at T3.
- Speed {times} (1 + 0.5 {times} min({u+03c3}, 1)): up to 6 {times} (T2) and 24 {times} (T3) the T1 rate.
- {9}Entanglement Medium{r} (T3) needs {u+03c3} {ge} 1 to start and pauses below it.
- {9}Degenerate Stellar Mixture{r} never needs bursts: Eye T6 needs it before any quasar exists.
The GUI and the scanner show the link line; OpenComputers bts_homogeny.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} your Homogeny shows a quasar link (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Planets Mode
desc: Planets mode is the Eye's {9}mode switch{r}: the Galaxy panel, or OpenComputers setMode("planets"). The galaxy chart in the slot picks the tier: Triangulum gives {9}3 slots{r}, the Milky Way 6. The planets field lights at once, with no collapse.
- Planet items (the dimension display blocks) go in the {9}slot bus{r}, the plinth's p input bus. They are read, never consumed. Taking a planet out of the slot bus abandons only that planet's run.
- One gauge (P, drift 1 {times} ({u+03b2} - 1), calm), no events, a quarter of the demand.
- Each planet runs at parallel 2^(N - k). Its success per parallel is (1 - 0.05 {times} rocket tier) {times} the field factor (Resonant and Stable 1, Strained 0.5, Critical 0).

- Each slot pays its run at the start (Hydrogen and Helium {times} parallel from the buffers, and its EU) and waits while it cannot (Slots [1]). A Breach fails the runs in flight and re-forms the field.
[warn]Switching the mode puts a lit galaxy out; it comes back only through the Magnetar Collapse.[/warn]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have run planets mode (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Companions
desc: {9}Star charts{r} of earlier objects (Sol to the magnetar) in the slot bus run beside the galaxy: {9}1 at T7, 2 at T8{r}.
- Each pays its own upkeep every cycle, in full, and makes its own product at the galaxy's yield.
- Each runs at parallel 2^(N - 1 - k) and adds a quarter of the demand and more noise on P.
- Slots [2]: a companion's upkeep is short.
[warn]Changing the companions re-forms the galaxy in place: the gauges go to 0 and the cycle in flight is lost.[/warn]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} a companion runs beside your galaxy (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Automating the Quasar
desc: The disc runs itself on two valves and two logic gates:

- A Directive Hatch on {9}Quasar: Disc{r} (Code mode, window 5). [1] {to} a valve of 10 units of the feed gas a second into a plain trim hatch (an AE2 fluid export bus with a redstone card, or a GT Fluid Regulator cover set to enable with signal). [2] {to} a valve of 10 units of Spatially Enlarged Fluid.
- (Disc [4] AND NOT the Eye's Galaxy Transition [8]) OR Galaxy Transition [4] {to} the quasar's Burst Control Hatch in Purge mode: one AND-NOT gate and one OR gate.
- ME stocking hatches in the 24 gas sockets, and f 1.0 in the GUI.
OpenComputers instead: bts_quasar.trim("gas" or "space", units), purge(), setFeed(f), setField(b), getDisc().
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} your quasar holds its disc on its own (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}A Galaxy That Runs Itself
desc: The {9}standard rig{r} takes a fresh 64 SM quasar and an Eye from T6 through T7 to T8 with nothing touched:
- Eye Field [1] {to} the Eye's Space valve (10 units into a Field hatch).
- {9}J1{r}: Field [2] / [1] as 15 / 8 / 0 (two emitter covers), OR Galaxy Transition [4] {to} 15, OR Slots [8] {to} 15.
- {9}J2{r}: Field [4] / [8]. {9}J3{r}: Events [1] / [2]; Slots [8] {to} its 75 % preset at T7.

- Transition [4] {to} push the next core into a plinth bus; Transition [1] {to} push the next chart; Status [1] {to} stock the charge; Galaxy Transition [1] {to} the Eye's Burst Control Hatch in Begin mode.

- Set {9}J1's out 1 limit{r} to {9}7.5 Bu/t{r} (7.5e13 EU/t) per parallel, times the time dial (the Junction's GUI, or junction.setLimit): J1 then steers the same few Bu/t into the Eye however big the quasar grows, and the rest goes to the crown. Without it, a quasar past about 200 SM floods the Eye through Mk II or bigger throats, test fire or not.
All binary like this (AE2-friendly), T8 runs about 90 % Resonant. Analog instead: the sensor's P (inverted, {pm}30), W and {u+039b} straight to J1, J2 and J3.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} your galaxy runs a full cycle untouched (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Scripting a Quasar
desc: With OpenComputers, an Adapter against a Beyond the Stars machine (the Eye, the Kerr, the quasar, a conduit element, a crown, a receptor port, the Homogeny, Reality Diffraction, a Directive or Sensor hatch) gives a component. Setters take one call a second (the field's step); a refused call returns nil and the reason.

- bts_quasar: getDisc, getBurst, getFeed, setFeed, setGas, setField, trim, purge, getLinks, getMilestones, getDirective; with a lattice also getBand, getIntake, getHoldUp, getBuffer, getOverdrive, getAnchor, getHorizon, setMassSetpoint, setOverdrive, setUnbound, shed;
- bts_eye: getState, getField, getBuffers, getEvent, getUnlock, getDirective, beginTransition, setDial, setFeed, setFeed8, setMode, trim, getSlots;
- bts_mouth and bts_mirror: getLink, getThroat, getUpkeep, setFuel, isOpen;
- bts_junction: getFlow, setRatio, setGain, setOut3, setLimit, setMode;
- bts_crown (getPower, getStream, getMk), bts_receptor (getDelivery), bts_homogeny, bts_reality, bts_kerr (getState().link), bts_directive and bts_sensor.
[note]Optional: the logic-gate rig needs no computer.[/note]
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you have read one of these from a computer (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Bursts into Power
desc: {9}1 Bu/t = 10{sup13} EU/t{r}. A 64 SM quasar at coils 3 makes about 2 Bu/t (2e13 EU/t, 20 trillion); the stream grows as M{sq}, and the hole grows with its disc up to the coil cap.

Sizing: G0 = {u+03bb} {times} a{sq} {times} b{sq} {times} (M/64){sq}. Never purging averages 1.11 {times} G0 {times} the jet yield, purging at flux 40 about 0.8. A good 1,024 SM quasar is worth about 5 to 10 {times} 10{u+00b9}{u+2075} EU/t, depending on how well its disc is held.
The NEI page Burst Thermaliser Crown lists each Mk's cap and EU/t.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} a crown feeds your network (tick the box).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Tier 14 (MAX)
desc: The last voltage tier. The Supermassive Lattice's L2 tier and the pack's own MAX quests work now. Eye T9, White Hole Matter, the MAX parts, the Reality machines and Eye T10 are {9}coming in a later update{r}: their quests are checkboxes until then.
{5}{l}THE PLAN{r}
- Eye T9 makes {9}White Hole Matter{r}, and every MAX part is built from it, so MAX parts arrive before T10.
- The Homogeny T3 and the two Reality machines make the {9}Universal Upgrade Core{r}.
- {9}Eye T10{r} makes Universium, and Universium opens the pack's Universium line in {1}The Endgame{r}.
{2}{l}DONE WHEN{r} you tick the box: this one is the chapter's introduction.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}T9 Pellets
desc: Pellets made from T6, T7 and T8 matter (Magnetar Matter, Ergomatter and Superdense Ergomatter, with the Homogeny's Degenerate Stellar Mixture), fired as a higher-GeV beam that powers and stabilises Eye T9.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Eye T9: White Hole
desc: Sgr A{ast}, the supermassive black hole at a galaxy's heart, with tidal disruption events to catch. Output: {9}White Hole Matter{r}. A planets mode will run 9 planets at once.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}White Hole Matter

tasks.what: a White Hole Matter fluid task

desc: Eye T9's harvest, and what every MAX part will be built from.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}The Homogeny T3
desc: The Homogeny's third tier: a tilted outer ring and its tail. It will mix at {9}16 parallels{r} (about one MAX amp) and add the last mix, {9}Entanglement Medium{r}: White Hole Matter + Superdense Ergomatter + Degenerate Stellar Mixture. Reality Diffraction splits it.
Entanglement Medium needs a quasar link at {u+03c3} {ge} 1; without it the run waits (see {c}A Quasar-Held Vortex{r}).

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Reality Diffraction
desc: A stack of glass drums with six Region Blades. Each run will split Entanglement Medium into six {9}Entangled Region{r} condensates (Hyperspace, Subspace, Forward Time, Reverse Time, Positive Mass, Negative Mass) and push them into a Bose-Einstein Condensate network: outside reality.
- Each region needs its own anchor fluid in its own socket, or its sixth is lost.
- Give the Reality machines their own BEC network: six extra condensates would clog every other Condensate Assembler.
- Its portal takes 6 GRB Receptor Ports: faster with a strong quasar link, paused with a weak one, {times} 1 with none (see {c}Riding the Rift{r}).
- A missing block, or a footprint chunk that is not loaded, pauses the machine: the run is kept and resumes by itself when the structure is whole. Chunk-load the whole footprint.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Reality Refab
desc: A tall vase of a machine. It will draw the six regions back out of the BEC network in lockstep and reassemble them, borrowing a linked Condensate Assembler's nanites. Its first job is the {9}Universal Upgrade Core{r}, which takes the Eye from T9 to T10.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}The Tenth Compression Tier
desc: Gallifreyan is TecTech's last Spacetime Compression Field Generator. The gate is 1 : 1, so Eye T10 needs a new, tenth tier.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}Eye T10: The Universe
desc: The Universe. A jump as big as the Nano Forge's T4. Output: {9}Universium{r}, and only here. It opens {1}The Endgame{r}.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}MAX Parts
desc: Every MAX part will be built from {9}White Hole Matter{r}, so MAX parts arrive before Eye T10. The four quests below group them: components and casings, power, materials, and the battery.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}MAX Components and Casings

tasks.what: the nine MAX components, the MAX CoAL casing and the MAX machine casing

desc: The MAX tier of GT's component set (motor, pump, conveyor, piston, robot arm, emitter, sensor, field generator and the rest), the MAX CoAL casing and the MAX machine casing, all from White Hole Matter.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}MAX Power

tasks.what: the MAX energy and dynamo hatches, laser source and target, wireless hatch

desc: The MAX energy and dynamo hatches, the MAX laser source and target hatches, and the MAX wireless hatch, all from White Hole Matter.

quests.name: {4}{l}{n}MAX Materials

tasks.what: the MAX superconductor, White Hole heating coil, glass and frame
